query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Forming a percolating, ∼5 vol % ductile-Ni intergranular network by electroless-plating each (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 powder particle with ≈1 µm Ni before hot-press consolidation will triple the bulk compressive strength and increase thermal conductivity at least four-fold while retaining ≥90 % of the parent alloy’s field- and pressure-driven caloric entropy change (|ΔS|).
generation.material_initial_state: Gas-atomised (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy powders, <45 µm, consolidated by hot pressing into a dense but brittle monolith that exhibits large magnetocaloric and barocaloric effects near 300 K yet cracks under <50 MPa compressive load.
generation.intervention: Electroless nickel deposition producing ~1 µm continuous Ni shells around each powder particle, followed by low-temperature (≤700 °C) hot pressing to yield a fully dense core–shell composite in which the Ni forms an interconnected ductile network.
generation.conditions: Operation at 250–350 K under cyclic (i) magnetic fields 0–2 T and/or (ii) uniaxial pressures 0–1 GPa; cycling frequency ≤1 Hz; atmosphere inert (Ar).
generation.structural_mediator: Interpenetrating Ni network located along former particle boundaries that supplies plastic compliance and high thermal-conductivity paths while leaving the HEA cores intact.
generation.mechanism:
1. Mechanical: the ductile Ni network blunts and bridges transformation-induced microcracks, redistributing stresses and raising fracture and compressive strengths.
2. Thermal: Ni (κ ≈ 90 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹) provides rapid heat spreading, decreasing local thermal gradients during adiabatic cycles.
3. Caloric retention: Because Ni occupies only grain-boundary volume (≤10 vol %), the first-order magnetostructural transition within the HEA cores—and thus the large |ΔS|—remains essentially unchanged; the Ni is magnetically active but its contribution is minor relative to the HEA, so overall ΔS is reduced by <10 %.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the unmodified bulk alloy: (a) room-temperature compressive strength increases from ~50 MPa to >150 MPa; (b) thermal conductivity rises from ~5 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ to ≥20 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹; (c) peak |ΔS| under 2 T or 1 GPa is ≥90 % of the baseline value (no more than 10 % loss); (d) samples survive ≥10⁴ magneto-/baro-caloric cycles with <5 % degradation versus catastrophic cracking of the baseline within ≤10 cycles.
generation.baseline: Hot-pressed monolithic (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 exhibiting ~50 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ |ΔS| at 2 T, κ ≈ 5 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, compressive strength <50 MPa, and cracking within the first few thermo-mechanical cycles.
generation.boundary: Ni volume fraction must remain ≤10 vol % and consolidation temperature ≤700 °C to avoid extensive Ni–HEA interdiffusion that would shift the transition temperature by >5 K or reduce |ΔS| by >10 %.
generation.uncertainty: Main risks are (i) interdiffusion of Ni altering the multicomponent phase equilibria, potentially broadening the first-order transition, and (ii) eddy-current heating of the Ni network at high-frequency field cycling; quantitative estimates are presently lacking.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two cylindrical specimens (Ø5 mm × 10 mm): (A) baseline hot-pressed HEA; (B) Ni-coated-particle composite pressed under identical conditions. Measure (1) room-temperature compressive strength (ASTM E9), (2) thermal conductivity (laser flash), (3) magnetic and barocaloric ΔS(T) curves (Maxwell relation) under 0–2 T and 0–1 GPa, and (4) cyclic durability over 10⁴ full magnetocaloric cycles at 1 Hz with simultaneous monitoring of cracking (acoustic emission and post-mortem micro-CT).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if specimen B shows ANY of: (i) compressive strength ≤100 MPa, OR (ii) κ ≤10 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, OR (iii) peak |ΔS| <90 % of specimen A, OR (iv) >10 % degradation of |ΔS| or structural failure before 10⁴ cycles.
